title: Calamansi Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Calamansi Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Calamansi nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, zinc and potassium in kalamansi, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Calamansi nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your kalamansi (calamansi) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, zinc, potassium, magnesium, boron, manganese, iron, phosphorus and copper. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, boron, manganese, iron and copper stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which calamansi nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Calamansi nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of kalamansi

Young leaves with yellow patches between green veins (mottle leaf), small, narrow and standing upright.

Fruit small, hard and lumpy with gum spots in the white peel. Leaves curl and shoot tips die, sending out many shoots.

Young full size leaves pale between the veins with broad dark green bands along the veins. Leaf size stays normal.

Newest leaves yellow to ivory with green veins. Worst in wet, poorly drained or limey spots.

Extra large, dark green leaves on long, soft, S shaped shoots, gum blisters at the nodes and twig dieback.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a calamansi nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest calamansi nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in calamansi

Leaves turn light green, then yellow, evenly over the whole tree with no clear pattern, starting with the older leaves. Old leaves fall early, so the canopy looks thin and hollow, and new leaves come out small, thin and pale. Twigs may die back, the top looks thin and bushy, and the tree flowers sparsely, with fewer and smaller fruit. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees after a heavy crop or heavy rains, and young trees that miss their regular feeding.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in kalamansi
Sandy soils with little organic matter, heavy rain or watering that leaches nitrogen, drought, very low or very high soil pH. Fresh straw or raw manure that ties nitrogen up as it rots.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency looks alike but starts on the young leaves, with veins that stay green. Late magnesium deficiency also yellows whole leaves, but leaves at an earlier stage show a green V at the base. To be sure, leaf test of 4 to 6 month old leaves from a flush on twigs without fruit, the way UF IFAS samples citrus, plus a soil test. A tree whose next flush greens up after fertilizer confirms it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

The DA ATI calamansi guide gives 50 to 100 grams of Ammonium sulfate or Urea per tree a month after planting and every four months after, 200 to 300 grams in the second year. From the fourth year a complete fertilizer with potash at 500 grams per tree, rising to 2 to 3 kg per tree three times a year at 8 to 10 years. For quick greening TNAU gives a Urea spray at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) every 15 days. UF IFAS advises low biuret urea for sprays.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, feed bearing trees three times a year: in the rainy season before flowering, two months after flowering and after harvest, as the ATI guide sets out.
Zinc deficiency in calamansi

Young leaves show it first: yellow patches between the veins, with an uneven green band along the midrib and main veins, called mottle leaf. As it gets worse the leaves turn pale yellow to almost white, come out small, narrow and pointed (little leaf), stand upright, and twigs die back. Fruit on these twigs stay small, with a smooth, pale, thin skin and little juice, and the tree flowers and sets less. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, at any age.
Why zinc deficiency happens in kalamansi
High pH and limed soils, soils high in phosphorus or given heavy phosphate, organic soils, and large, frequent doses of poultry manure. Shortage of magnesium or copper can also cut zinc uptake.
How to tell it apart

Citrus greening (huanglongbing, HLB) is the big look alike. A UPLB survey in Oriental Mindoro found HLB in 150 of 155 calamansi trees tested, with a blotchy mottle and yellowing between the veins similar to zinc deficiency. To be sure, do the pen test, then spray zinc on a few branches: if the next flush comes out green and normal sized, it was zinc. If the blotches stay uneven or the tree keeps declining, send leaves for an HLB laboratory test (the UPLB team used PCR).
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray zinc on the young flush when the leaves are two thirds to almost fully expanded, as UF IFAS advises. Repeat on each major flush in bad cases, because zinc does not move on to later flushes. TNAU gives Zinc sulfate at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) mixed with 1 percent lime (10 grams per liter), every two weeks. Zinc on the soil rarely pays on acid soils and does not work on limey ones.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep the pH below 6.5, avoid heavy phosphate and too much poultry manure, and include zinc in regular sprays.
Potassium deficiency in calamansi

The edges of older leaves turn pale yellow or bronze, and with time the yellowing spreads over the leaf. Growth slows, leaves drop around flowering, and new leaves are small and wrinkled, with scorched tips and small brown resin spots. Twigs may die back. Fruit stay small with a smooth, thin peel and may split from the blossom end or drop. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees during fruit growth, most of all under heavy crops.
Why potassium deficiency happens in kalamansi
Acid and sandy soils, heavy rain or watering that leaches potash, drought, soils rich in magnesium. High nitrogen rates on heavy crops without enough potash.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on older leaves, but it leaves a green V at the base of the leaf. Salt or fertilizer burn scorches leaf edges on leaves of all ages after a heavy dose or salty water. To be sure, leaf test of 4 to 6 month old leaves from twigs without fruit. A soil test for potash, magnesium and calcium together.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or a complete fertilizer in the ring in split doses, following the soil test. From the fourth year the DA ATI guide gives a complete fertilizer with potash at 500 grams per tree, rising to 2 to 3 kg per tree three times a year at 8 to 10 years. For a quick fix TNAU gives a Potassium nitrate spray at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) every two weeks.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, match potash to nitrogen, especially on heavy bearing trees, and never feed nitrogen alone for long.
Magnesium deficiency in calamansi

It shows on mature leaves close to the fruit. A yellowish green blotch starts near the base of the leaf on each side of the midrib and grows until only the tip and a V shaped area at the base, pointing up the midrib, stay green. In bad cases the whole leaf turns yellow to bronze and drops, heavily fruiting branches lose most of their leaves, and those twigs may die. Seedy fruit like calamansi draw more magnesium than seedless kinds. You see it most at this stage: during fruit growth, on heavily bearing branches. The new flush may look normal while older leaves near the fruit yellow.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in kalamansi
Sandy and acid soils, soils rich in potash or given heavy potash, and cold, wet periods. On limey soils, the high calcium also holds magnesium back.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole tree evenly with no pattern. Potassium deficiency bronzes the leaf edges. To be sure, leaf test and a soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium together.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

On acid to neutral soils, Dolomite corrects mild cases and gives lime too. Where the soil test shows low magnesium, UF IFAS gives magnesium at a rate equal to 20 percent of the nitrogen rate. Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) or Kieserite can supply it. On limey soils use magnesium sprays on the leaves.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite when liming and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Boron deficiency in calamansi

Fruit stay small, hard and misshapen with a lumpy surface, many drop. Dark gum spots form in the white inner peel and sometimes in the core. Young leaves wilt early, show water soaked spots, curl, and the veins can split and turn corky. The growing tip dies, so the shoot sends out many side shoots and the tree looks bushy. You see it most at this stage: flowering, fruit set and fruit growth, often after a long dry spell.
Why boron deficiency happens in kalamansi
Sandy and alkaline soils low in organic matter, high nitrogen or calcium, cold wet weather and drought. UF IFAS also sees it where growers use only high analysis fertilizers with no micronutrients.
How to tell it apart

Citrus greening also gives corky veins and small, lopsided fruit that color unevenly. Use the pen test on the leaves. To be sure, leaf test and soil test for boron. Cut a few fruit: brown or gummy spots in the white peel point to boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

TNAU gives a Borax spray at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter). UF IFAS advises boron every year where it is needed, either on the soil or as a spray but never both, because citrus is easily burned by too much.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use fertilizers that carry micronutrients, not straight high analysis grades only, keep organic matter up and water during long dry spells.
Manganese deficiency in calamansi

Young leaves show a fine network of green veins on a lighter green background, less sharp than with zinc or iron. By full size the pattern is clear: dark green bands along the midrib and main veins with light green areas between. In bad cases white spots form between the veins, leaves drop early and the tree looks weak. Leaves keep their normal size and shape. You see it most at this stage: on young and newly matured flushes. Mild signs on new shoots may fade as the flush hardens.
Why manganese deficiency happens in kalamansi
It happens on both acid soils, where manganese leaches, and on limey or overlimed soils, where it is locked up. Sandy and organic soils and cold, wet periods add to it.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency makes the leaves small, narrow and pointed. Iron deficiency is paler, with a finer net, on the newest leaves. To be sure, look at the leaves more than once over several weeks before acting, since mild signs can pass. Then do a leaf test and a soil test for pH and manganese.
What to apply for manganese deficiency

TNAU gives a Manganese sulfate spray at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) every two weeks. Spray the new flush when the leaves are two thirds to fully expanded. UF IFAS notes that a little low biuret urea in the spray helps uptake. On acid soils manganese sulfate can also go on the soil. On limey soils use sprays only.

Sold here with manganese: **Manganese Sulfate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (31 percent manganese), **Tierramino Mn** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (12 percent manganese and 7 percent N), **Multimate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (1.8 percent Mn, 2.8 percent Zn, 4 percent N, 4.5 percent S (w/v)) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid overliming and include manganese with zinc in the regular spray program.
Iron deficiency in calamansi

It always starts on the youngest leaves: yellow green, then pale yellow between veins that stay green, sometimes with even the fine veins green like a net. In bad cases the whole leaf turns ivory, new leaves are small, thin and fragile and drop early. Twigs die back at the top and edge of the canopy while older leaves stay green. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, especially in the rainy season on wet soils.
Why iron deficiency happens in kalamansi
High pH and limey soils, too much water, poor drainage, cool soils, salty soils, high phosphorus. Copper built up in old orchard soil.
How to tell it apart

Manganese and zinc shortages often come with it, since all three get worse at high pH. Flood damage to roots and copper toxicity both first show as iron chlorosis, so check the roots and the spray history. To be sure, soil test for pH, and for copper on old orchard land, and check drainage and the roots.
What to apply for iron deficiency

Fix drainage first. UF IFAS reports trees helped or cured just by better irrigation and drainage. On high pH soils apply an iron chelate (Fe EDDHA) to the soil. UF does not recommend iron sprays on citrus, because they green the leaf only in specks and can burn. TNAU does give a Ferrous sulfate spray at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter), twice, two weeks apart, as a quick try.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, plant on well drained ground or raised beds, avoid overliming, and keep the pH near neutral.
Phosphorus deficiency in calamansi

Older leaves lose their deep green and turn dull, small and narrow, with a purplish or bronze cast. In bad cases small brown to bronze freckles join up along the main veins. Leaves and fruit drop early, flowering and fruit set are poor, and roots stay short. Fruit are rough, with a coarse, thick peel, a hollow core and more acid. You see it most at this stage: young trees and new plantings on land never fertilized. Rare in trees fed regularly for years.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in kalamansi
Strongly acid soils where iron and aluminium lock phosphorus up, very alkaline soils, low organic matter, cold wet soil and weak roots.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency gives the opposite fruit: small, with a smooth, thin peel. Nitrogen deficiency gives evenly pale leaves without bronze freckles. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer, following the soil test. The DA ATI guide uses ammophos (16 20 0) with potash once trees bear. UF IFAS notes that superphosphate suits soils of any pH and adds sulfur. Warns not to use DAP (18 46 0) on alkaline soils. Lime very acid soils so the phosphorus stays available.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole and in the first years, and add compost.
Copper deficiency in calamansi

The first sign is unusually large, dark green leaves with the midrib bowed up, on long, soft, angular shoots that droop in an S shape. Small blisters of clear gum form at the nodes, and reddish brown gum breaks out on older twigs. Twigs then die back from the tip and push out a bunch of weak buds. Fruit can show brown gum stains and split. You see it most at this stage: young trees in new plantings, and trees pushed with heavy nitrogen.
Why copper deficiency happens in kalamansi
New plantings on sandy or organic soils never farmed before, limey soils, and heavy nitrogen feeding. It is rare where copper fungicides are sprayed.
How to tell it apart

Gummosis, which the DA ATI guide describes as dark, sticky gum oozing from branches and trunk, is a bark disease. Copper deficiency gum sits in small blisters on young twigs and as stains on the fruit. To be sure, check the spray record: if copper fungicides are used, copper deficiency is unlikely. A soil test on new land helps.
What to apply for copper deficiency

UF IFAS reports near immediate recovery from a copper spray at flowering. TNAU gives Copper sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) every two weeks. Try it on a few branches first, since plain copper sulfate can burn soft leaves. Cut back excess nitrogen. Do not overdo copper: it builds up in the soil and below pH 5.5 it can kill roots.

Sold here with copper: **Omex Zynergy** by Jardine Distribution, Inc. (3.75 percent zinc and 2.11 percent copper), **Grower's Choice Copper Sulphate Pentahydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (25 percent copper and 12 percent sulfur), **Agsmart Copper Sulphate** by AgSmart Corporation (25 percent copper and 12 percent sulfur) and **Liquid Chelate Copper w/ Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent copper and 2 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [copper deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/copper-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, on new sandy land UF IFAS adds copper to the fertilizer at 2.5 percent of the nitrogen rate.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any calamansi nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your kalamansi needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Calamansi nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my kalamansi leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole tree turns light green to yellow, old leaves drop early and the canopy thins. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in calamansi?
items.a: The DA ATI calamansi guide gives 50 to 100 grams of Ammonium sulfate or Urea per tree a month after planting and every four months after, 200 to 300 grams in the second year. From the fourth year a complete fertilizer with potash at 500 grams per tree, rising to 2 to 3 kg per tree three times a year at 8 to 10 years.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes zinc deficiency in calamansi?
items.a: Spray zinc on the young flush when the leaves are two thirds to almost fully expanded, as UF IFAS advises. Repeat on each major flush in bad cases, because zinc does not move on to later flushes.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in calamansi?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or a complete fertilizer in the ring in split doses, following the soil test. From the fourth year the DA ATI guide gives a complete fertilizer with potash at 500 grams per tree, rising to 2 to 3 kg per tree three times a year at 8 to 10 years.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my kalamansi lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the calamansi nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
